sections.text: Eighteen trials test C5 inhibition in myasthenia gravis, including fifteen in Phase 3, one in Phase 4, and two in Phase 2.
Eculizumab, ravulizumab, and zilucoplan are approved for use in myasthenia gravis according to the site_target data.
One Phase 2 trial of eculizumab in refractory generalized myasthenia gravis was terminated due to slow enrollment.
Eculizumab and ravulizumab carry FDA black box warnings for serious meningococcal infections, including cases despite vaccination.
A 2026 case report describes rapid and durable improvement in two patients with refractory myasthenic crisis or impending crisis treated with zilucoplan.
Another 2026 case report details fulminant meningococcal meningitis in a vaccinated patient receiving ravulizumab, highlighting the persistent risk despite preventive measures.
The site_risk tool reports a median stop risk of 0.279 for ongoing C5 inhibition trials in myasthenia gravis.
C5 inhibitors are part of a broader landscape including FcRn antagonists and rituximab, with recent reviews discussing sequencing and comparative effectiveness.

read: Mechanism evidence: C5 inhibition shows efficacy in refractory and acute myasthenia gravis, including life-threatening crises.
Competitive position: Multiple approved drugs and late-phase trials indicate a mature, competitive class with known safety risks.
Open questions: How to optimally sequence C5 inhibitors with other biologics, and how to mitigate meningococcal infection risk despite vaccination.
would_change: New safety signals, especially from ongoing Phase 3 or 4 trials, could increase the stop risk and shift the stance to mixed or against.
Demonstrated efficacy in head-to-head comparisons with other mechanisms like FcRn antagonists would strengthen the competitive position.
